question_text: What is meant by hydroboration-oxidation reaction? Illustrate it with an example.

question_image.description: Diagram illustrating the hydroboration-oxidation reaction process.

answer_text: The addition of borane followed by oxidation is known as the hydroboration-oxidation reaction. For example, propan-1-ol is produced by the hydroboration-oxidation reaction of propene. In this reaction, propene reacts with diborane (BH3) to form trialkyl borane as an addition product. This addition product is oxidized to alcohol by hydrogen peroxide in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide.
final_answer: Thus, hydroboration-oxidation converts propene to propan-1-ol.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the hydroboration-oxidation mechanism and its application.

(i) Kolbe's reaction.
(ii) Reimer-Tiemann reaction.
(iii) Williamson ether synthesis.
(iv) Unsymmetrical ether.

question_image.description: Mathematical representation related to the reactions discussed.

parts.part_text: Kolbe's reaction: When phenol is treated with sodium hydroxide, sodium phenoxide is produced. This sodium phenoxide when treated with carbon dioxide, followed by acidification, undergoes electrophilic substitution to give ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid as the main product.
parts.answer_text: Kolbe's reaction involves the formation of ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid from phenol and sodium hydroxide.

steps.description: Treat phenol with sodium hydroxide to form sodium phenoxide.
React sodium phenoxide with carbon dioxide and acidify to obtain ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid.

parts.final_answer: Thus, Kolbe's reaction produces ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid.

parts.part_text: Reimer-Tiemann reaction: When phenol is treated with chloroform (CHCl) in the presence of sodium hydroxide, a -CHO group is introduced at the ortho position of the benzene ring.
parts.answer_text: The Reimer-Tiemann reaction introduces a -CHO group at the ortho position of phenol.

steps.description: Treat phenol with chloroform and sodium hydroxide.
Hydrolyze the intermediate to produce salicyclaldehyde.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, the Reimer-Tiemann reaction yields salicyclaldehyde.

parts.part_text: Williamson ether synthesis: This is a laboratory method to prepare symmetrical and unsymmetrical ethers by allowing alkyl halides to react with sodium alkoxides.
parts.answer_text: Williamson ether synthesis involves the reaction of alkyl halides with sodium alkoxides.

steps.description: React alkyl halides with sodium alkoxides.
Ensure primary alkyl halides for better results.

parts.final_answer: Thus, Williamson ether synthesis is effective for preparing ethers.

parts.part_text: Unsymmetrical ether: An unsymmetrical ether is an ether where two groups on the two sides of an oxygen atom differ.
parts.answer_text: An example of an unsymmetrical ether is ethyl methyl ether.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, ethyl methyl ether is an example of an unsymmetrical ether.

question_text: Illustrate with examples the limitations of Williamson synthesis for the preparation of certain types of ethers.

question_image.description: Diagram illustrating the limitations of Williamson synthesis with alkoxide ions and alkyl halides.

answer_text: The reaction of Williamson synthesis involves S N 2 attack of an alkoxide ion on a primary alkyl halide. But if secondary or tertiary alkyl halides are taken in place of primary alkyl halides, then elimination would compete over substitution. As a result, alkenes would be produced. This is because alkoxides are nucleophiles as well as strong bases.
final_answer: Thus, the limitations arise due to the competing elimination reactions with secondary and tertiary alkyl halides.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of reaction mechanisms and conditions for ether synthesis.

question_images.description: Diagram illustrating the limitations of Williamson synthesis with alkoxide ions and alkyl halides.

question_text: How is 1-propoxypropane synthesised from propan-1-ol? Write mechanism of this reaction.

question_image.description: Mechanism of the synthesis of 1-propoxypropane from propan-1-ol.

answer_text: 1-propoxypropane can be synthesized from propan-1-ol by dehydration. Propan-1-ol undergoes dehydration in the presence of protic acids (such as H2SO4, H3PO4) to give 1-propoxypropane. The mechanism of this reaction involves the following three steps: Step 1: Protonation, Step 2: Nucleophilic attack, Step 3: Deprotonation.

steps.description: Protonation of propan-1-ol to form a better leaving group.
Nucleophilic attack by the alkoxide ion on the protonated alcohol.
Deprotonation to form 1-propoxypropane.

final_answer: Thus, 1-propoxypropane is formed through dehydration of propan-1-ol.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of reaction mechanisms and multi-step synthesis.

subject: chemistry
question_text: Preparation of ethers by acid dehydration of secondary or tertiary alcohols is not a suitable method. Give reason.
answer_text: The formation of ethers by dehydration of alcohol is a bimolecular reaction (S N 2) involving the attack of an alcohol molecule on a protonated alcohol molecule. In the method, the alkyl group should be unhindered. In case of secondary or tertiary alcohols, the alkyl group is hindered. As a result, elimination dominates substitution. Hence, in place of ethers, alkenes are formed.
final_answer: Therefore, secondary and tertiary alcohols lead to elimination rather than ether formation.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of reaction mechanisms and steric hindrance.

question_text: Explain the fact that in aryl alkyl ethers (i) The alkoxy group activates the benzene ring towards electrophilic substitution and (ii) It directs the incoming substituents to ortho and para positions in benzene ring.
answer_text: In aryl alkyl ethers, due to the +R effect of the alkoxy group, the electron density in the benzene ring increases. Thus, benzene is activated towards electrophilic substitution by the alkoxy group. It can also be observed from the resonance structures that the electron density increases more at the ortho and para positions than at the meta position. As a result, the incoming substituents are directed to the ortho and para positions in the benzene ring.
final_answer: Thus, the alkoxy group activates the benzene ring and directs substituents to ortho and para positions.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of resonance and electrophilic substitution.
